gist: Manchester United need stability rather than constant managerial changes.

The club should follow Arsenal's blueprint with Mikel Arteta and give time.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester United appointed Michael Carrick as interim manager in January. He experienced a strong start, finishing third and securing Champions League places, but performances have since levelled off. Following a defeat by Como in the Champions League, captain Bruno Fernandes made comments that raised concerns, and defender Lisandro Martinez publicly questioned the club's recruitment strategy.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Constant managerial changes and huge failures in recruitment have left United struggling. The squad lacks the required character and ability across outfield positions to win major titles, and managing players with inflated opinions of themselves presents a major challenge.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: United must take their medicine, reset their identity, and back Michael Carrick rather than changing their manager again. Achieving success will take time and stability.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton and Tom McKibbin announced they are leaving LIV Golf. This follows departures from Jon Rahm, Louis Oosthuizen, Abraham Ancer and David Puig, while Sergio Garcia, Thomas Pieters, Laurie Canter and Adrian Meronk are unlikely to stay. The Saudi Public Investment Fund withdrew backing in April and LIV filed for bankruptcy protection last month.

sections.heading: Why it matters
